quick: With or without food, any time
summary: Atorvastatin is a potent HMG-CoA reductase inhibitor that lowers LDL-C and reduces cardiovascular events in primary and secondary prevention. Dosed 10-80 mg once daily with or without food. Key risks are myopathy and rare rhabdomyolysis.
indications: Primary hyperlipidemia and mixed dyslipidemia (adjunct to diet)
Reduce risk of MI, stroke, revascularization and angina in adults with multiple CHD risk factors without clinically evident CHD
Reduce risk of MI and stroke in adults with type 2 diabetes plus CHD risk factors
Secondary prevention in patients with clinically evident CHD
Heterozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HeFH) in adults and children >=10 years
Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia (HoFH) as adjunct to other lipid-lowering treatments

dosage.n: Start 40 mg if LDL-C reduction >45% required

dosage.d: 10-20 mg once daily; up to 80 mg/day

admin: Take orally once daily at any time of day
May be taken with or without food
Assess LDL-C as early as 4 weeks after start and adjust dose
Reduce dose with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors per label limits
moa: Competitively inhibits HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme converting HMG-CoA to mevalonate in hepatic cholesterol synthesis. Reduced intracellular cholesterol upregulates LDL receptors, increasing clearance of LDL-C and lowering plasma LDL, total cholesterol and triglycerides.

absolute: Acute liver failure or decompensated cirrhosis
relative: Predisposition to myopathy (hypothyroidism, renal impairment, age >65, low body weight)

preg: Discontinue when pregnancy is recognized. Cholesterol and statin-derived products are important for fetal development; benefit of continuing in pregnancy is unlikely to outweigh risk.
lact: Not recommended during breastfeeding due to potential to disrupt infant lipid metabolism. Discontinue drug or nursing.
renal: No dose adjustment required; renal disease does not affect plasma concentrations or LDL-C response. Plasma levels are not lowered by hemodialysis.
hepatic: Contraindicated in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevations. Use caution and monitor LFTs in chronic liver disease or heavy alcohol use.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (clarithromycin, itraconazole, HIV protease inhibitors) - increase atorvastatin levels and myopathy risk; limit dose
moderate: Other fibrates and niacin - increased myopathy risk
Oral contraceptives - increased norethindrone/ethinyl estradiol levels
minor: Antacids - modest decrease in atorvastatin concentration
Rifampin - reduced atorvastatin exposure if staggered
interactions.food: Grapefruit juice (large amounts) increases exposure; avoid excessive intake.
interactions.alcohol: Limit alcohol; heavy use increases hepatotoxicity risk.
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate transaminases and creatine kinase.

emergency: Rhabdomyolysis (severe muscle pain, weakness, dark urine)

monitoring: Lipid panel at baseline and 4-12 weeks after initiation/dose change
Liver enzymes at baseline; repeat if clinically indicated
Creatine kinase if unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness
counsel: Take once daily at any time, consistent with or without food
Report unexplained muscle pain, tenderness or weakness promptly
Avoid large amounts of grapefruit juice
Inform provider if pregnant or planning pregnancy
pearls: Can be taken at any time of day unlike short-acting statins
Preferred statin in moderate renal impairment
missed: Take the missed dose when remembered unless it is close to the next dose; do not double up. If more than 12 hours have passed, skip and resume the regular schedule.
overdose: No specific antidote; treat symptomatically and supportively. Due to extensive protein binding, hemodialysis is not expected to enhance clearance. Monitor for muscle and liver effects.
